sources.title: Haas boss Komatsu lashes out at 'nonsense' Bearman salary rumours
Furious Komatsu dismisses 'nonsense' reports of Bearman demanding £5m salary

en.title: Komatsu dismisses Bearman salary demand rumors
en.dek: Haas boss denies reports of Oliver Bearman seeking a £5m annual salary.
facts: Komatsu, Haas team principal, denied reports of a £5m annual salary demand by Oliver Bearman.
Bearman, 21, said he wants to continue with Haas.
Haas announced Rafael Camara will replace Esteban Ocon in 2027.
Bearman’s contract expires at the end of the 2026 season.
Both parties say they are working toward a deal but have not disclosed details.
body: Komatsu, Haas team principal, denied reports that Oliver Bearman demanded a £5m annual salary. He said the claim was invented to generate clicks and that he had no idea where it came from.
Bearman, 21-year-old British driver, said he wants to continue with Haas. He added that the team is working on finalising details and that his goal is to stay with Haas.
Haas announced that Rafael Camara will replace Esteban Ocon in 2027. The lack of a confirmed extension for Bearman has led to speculation about the contract talks.
The contract for Bearman expires at the end of the 2026 season. Both parties have expressed confidence that a deal will be reached, but Komatsu declined to reveal the details preventing an agreement.
en.context: Bearman’s future has been in focus after Haas confirmed Camara for 2027. The driver’s contract is up at end 2026. Rumors about salary demands have surfaced.

problemsFixed: Incorrect salary figure used (£5m instead of six million euros).
